channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Gold price wilts as Oil shock puts CPI in Fed crosshairs
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) registers losses of over 0.44% on Tuesday amid a light economic docket in the US, due to a narrative dominated by the US-Iran conflict, higher Oil prices and traders bracing for the release of US inflation reports, with the PPI expected on Thursday, followed by the next day’s CPI.

item.title: Euro: Upside bias within defined range against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann analysts report that EUR/USD was little changed around 1.1620 on Monday, but note a slight pickup in upward momentum.

item.title: Euro rebounds against British Pound on diverging ECB-BoE interest rate paths
item.description: EUR/GBP rebounds on Tuesday after slipping to a six-day low earlier in the day. The recovery comes as the British Pound (GBP) weakens against most of its major peers following cautious remarks from Bank of England (BoE) Governor Andrew Bailey.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Policy scenarios favor stronger JPY against US Dollar – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad highlights that USD/JPY briefly hit a seven‑month low near 152.89 before rebounding above 154.00, with support around 152.00 and resistance at 155.00.

item.title: British Pound: Supportive BoE outlook with range trade against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret describe GBP/USD as slightly softer but supported by expectations of further Bank of England (BoE) tightening into year-end.

item.title: The Japanese Yen spikes and unwinds on the best pay data in decades
item.description: USD/JPY holds just below 154.50 on Tuesday, unchanged on the day after a 153-pip round trip. The pair traded well over a Yen lower on the strongest Japanese pay data since 1997 and has bought back all of it.

item.title: Canadian Dollar trims gains as risk aversion supports US Dollar despite higher Oil prices
item.description: USD/CAD rebounds on Tuesday after hitting an intraday low of 1.3760 and trades around 1.3790 at the time of writing, down 0.18% on the day.

item.title: The Euro's rate hike does not come with a gas cargo
item.description: EUR/USD holds above 1.1600 on Tuesday after a session that has covered 28 pips and left the pair half a pip from where it opened. European gas hit a three-year high on the same clock, and the European Central Bank (ECB) is expected to raise the deposit rate on Thursday.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average is paying for a sixth day of Crude Oil
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average trades near 52,900, roughly 190 points lower, in the first session since Friday. Crude Oil has risen for six days running and the two-year Treasury yield sits at its highest since January 2025. Neither is an equity story by itself.

item.title: NY Fed Survey of Consumers shows inflation relief, jobs-market unease
item.description: The New York Federal Reserve (Fed) released on Tuesday the August Survey of Consumer Expectations, in which households' inflation expectations dipped in the medium term, while expectations about the labor market remained mixed, as unemployment and job-finding deteriorated, while job losses and quit

item.title: Colombian Peso: Downside risk bias against US Dollar – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities notes that the Colombian Peso (COP) has been a top high-yield performer but sees its supportive mix of tight monetary and loose fiscal policy fading.

item.title: British Pound edges higher as Bailey calms recession fears
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) registers modest gains of over 0.08% on Tuesday as Bank of England (BoE) policymakers testify before the UK Treasury Select Committee, while a light economic docket in the US keeps the Greenback with a negative tone.

item.title: Australian Dollar holds firm on hawkish RBA stance, softer US Dollar
item.description: AUD/USD holds firm on Tuesday as the US Dollar (USD) struggles to gain traction, while the Reserve Bank of Australia’s (RBA) hawkish stance further supports the Australian Dollar (AUD).

item.title: US Dollar: Fed hold tempers dollar rebound – NBC
item.description: National Bank of Canada's (NBC) Stéfane Marion and Kyle Dahms note that the US Dollar (USD) has weakened broadly in Q3 even as the United States (US) economy remains at full employment.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Uptrend resumes with fair value focus against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note that the Canadian Dollar (CAD) is trading close to its fundamental equilibrium, with USD/CAD hovering near fair value around 1.38.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Bullish momentum extends against US Dollar – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Kenneth Broux highlights a sharp USD/JPY pullback, with the pair breaking key graphical support at 155 and trading below its 200-day moving average. The bank flags resistance near 156.25 and downside objectives at 152.00/151.60 and 149.50.

item.title: "Risks to inflation are to upside": BoE's Bailey sounds a cautious note
item.description: Bank of England (BoE) Governor Andrew Bailey said on Tuesday that he does not think the United Kingdom (UK) economy is on the verge of a recession, with the latest data showing slightly stronger activity, according to Reuters.

item.title: South African Rand: Gold prices support ZAR against US Dollar – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities remains constructive on South African Rand (ZAR), noting that domestic headwinds have failed to generate sustained weakness and that USD/ZAR’s downtrend remains intact.

item.title: Euro: ECB expectations support EUR against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret report that the Euro (EUR) is little changed near the low 1.16s as markets await Thursday’s European Central Bank (ECB) meeting, where a 25 bps hike and a hawkish tone are anticipated.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: Bulls struggle below the 100-day SMA
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) pulls back on Tuesday after failing to hold its earlier advance. At the time of writing, the metal trades around $66 after reaching an intraday high near $67.19.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar retreats as Chinese imports fall short of expectations
item.description: NZD/USD declines 0.37% on Tuesday, trading around 0.5855 at the time of writing. The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) remains under pressure following the release of mixed trade data from China, New Zealand’s largest trading partner.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Carry unwind boosts gains against US Dollar - DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Philip Wee notes that the Japanese Yen (JPY) has become the best-performing US Dollar Index (DXY) currency in 2026, with USD/JPY falling below its end-2025 level of 156.70.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Loonie rally pauses before fresh gains - NBC
item.description: National Bank of Canada's (NBC) Marion and Dahms highlight a strong Canadian Dollar (CAD) rally in Q3, driven by positive data and higher Oil and Gold prices, which pushed USD/CAD briefly below 1.38. They warn that new U.S. tariffs and trade uncertainty raise downside risks to Canadian growth.

item.title: Copper: Record prices and Chile supply issues – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Norman Liebke highlights that LME 3‑month Copper has set a new all‑time high above USD 14,530 per ton, supported by strong US demand and anticipated import tariffs.

item.title: Gold trades lower despite weaker US Dollar as Fed hike bets weigh
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) remains on the back foot during American trading hours on Tuesday, even as the US Dollar (USD) remains on the defensive. Rising Oil prices and expectations of a Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike weigh on the precious metal.

item.title: Brazilian Real: Election risks keep pressure on BRL against US Dollar – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities highlights that BRL faces elevated election-related risks, with USD/BRL having tested its 200-day SMA resistance over the past month. Drawing parallels with 2014, the bank sees risks skewed toward higher USD/BRL as markets remain concerned about Brazil’s fiscal outlook.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Strong jobs and CPI risks – BNY
item.description: BNY Markets strategist John Velis says a strong United States (US) jobs report has pushed expectations for a September Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike back above 60%, despite Governor Christopher Waller’s more cautious comments.

item.title: Euro holds steady as US Dollar struggles for traction
item.description: EUR/USD trades virtually flat near 1.1623 during American trading hours on Tuesday. The US Dollar (USD) struggles to hold its earlier gains, helping the Euro (EUR) recover from its intraday low.

item.title: European Central Bank: Clients see higher peak and later cuts – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank’s Mark Wall and Michael Kirker report that survey respondents expect the European Central Bank (ECB) to continue hiking, with a strong bias toward another move in September and a terminal rate between 2.50% and 3.00%.

item.title: US Dollar: Crude rally and CPI risks shape path – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes that Brent Oil’s surge toward $100 is pressuring stocks and bonds while giving the Dollar a modest lift. However, he stresses that Friday’s US August Consumer Price Index (CPI) will be decisive for the Federal Reserve’s September 16 meeting.
